messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: Writebook shows a live "being edited" indicator in a page's editor: while one
person saves, everyone else with the page open sees who is editing. But a
collaborator removed from the book keeps receiving those pushes: an editor
left open while they still had access keeps showing who is editing — presence
payloads, editor names included, for a page they can no longer edit. The
payload must not go out on a channel a removed collaborator can still be
listening on.

Fix it without breaking the indicator.


You can execute bash commands and edit files to implement the necessary changes.

module Book::Accessable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_many :accesses, dependent: :destroy
    scope :with_everyone_access, -> { where(everyone_access: true) }
  end

  class_methods do
    def accessable_or_published(user: Current.user)
      if user.present?
        accessable_or_published_books
      else
        published
      end
    end

    def accessable_or_published_books(user: Current.user)
      user.books.or(published).distinct
    end
  end

  def accessable?(user: Current.user)
    accesses.exists?(user: user)
  end

  def editable?(user: Current.user)
    access_for(user: user)&.editor? || user&.administrator?
  end

  def access_for(user: Current.user)
    accesses.find_by(user: user)
  end

  def update_access(editors:, readers:)
    editors = Set.new(editors)
    readers = Set.new(everyone_access? ? User.active.ids : readers)

    all = editors + readers
    all_accesses = all.collect { |user_id|
      { user_id: user_id, level: editors.include?(user_id) ? :editor : :reader }
    }

    accesses.upsert_all(all_accesses, unique_by: [ :book_id, :user_id ])
    accesses.where.not(user_id: all).delete_all
  end
end

  end

      format.md
    end
  end

  end

    update_accesses(@book)
    remove_cover if params[:remove_cover] == "true"

    redirect_to book_slug_url(@book)
  end

  def destroy
    @book.destroy

    redirect_to root_url
  end

      @book = Book.accessable_or_published.find params[:id]
    end

    def set_users
      @users = User.active.ordered
    end

    def ensure_editable
      head :forbidden unless @book.editable?
    end

        require_authentication
      end
    end

    end

      readers = [ Current.user.id, *params[:reader_ids]&.map(&:to_i) ]

    before_action :set_book
    before_action :set_leaf, :set_leafable, only: %i[ show edit update destroy ]
  end

  private
    def set_book
      @book = Book.accessable_or_published.find(params[:book_id])
    end

    def set_leaf

    end

    def set_leafable

      controller_leafable_name.constantize
    end

    def instance_name

      resource :join_code, only: :create
      resource :custom_styles, only: %i[ edit update ]
    end
  end

  resources :books, except: %i[ index show ] do
    resource :publication, controller: "books/publications", only: %i[ show edit update ]
    resource :bookmark, controller: "books/bookmarks", only: :show

    scope module: "books" do
      namespace :leaves do
        resources :moves, only: :create
      end

      resource :search

    resources :sections
    resources :pictures
    resources :pages

  get "/:book_id/:book_slug/:id/:slug", to: "leafables#show", constraints: { book_id: /\d+/, id: /\d+/ }, as: :slugged_leafable

  end

  direct :edit_leafable do |leaf, options|
    route_for "edit_book_#{leaf.leafable_name}", leaf.book, leaf, options

  end

  end

    book = Book.create! book_params
    update_accesses(book)

    redirect_to book_slug_url(book)
  end

  def show
    @leaves = @book.leaves.active.with_leafables.positioned

    respond_to do |format|
      format.html
      format.md
    end
  end

  def edit
  end

  def update
    @book.update(book_params)
    update_accesses(@book)
    remove_cover if params[:remove_cover] == "true"

    redirect_to book_slug_url(@book)
  end

  def destroy
    @book.destroy

    redirect_to root_url
  end

  private
    def set_book
      @book = Book.accessable_or_published.find params[:id]
    end

    def set_users
      @users = User.active.ordered
    end

    def ensure_editable
      head :forbidden unless @book.editable?
    end

    def ensure_index_is_not_empty
      if !signed_in? && Book.published.none?
        require_authentication
      end
    end

    def book_params
      params.require(:book).permit(:title, :subtitle, :author, :cover, :remove_cover, :everyone_access, :theme)
    end

    def update_accesses(book)
      editors = [ Current.user.id, *params[:editor_ids]&.map(&:to_i) ]
      readers = [ Current.user.id, *params[:reader_ids]&.map(&:to_i) ]

      book.update_access(editors: editors, readers: readers)
    end

    def remove_cover
      @book.cover.purge
    end
end

  "output_head": "# The streams channel delivers all the turbo-stream actions created (primarily) through <tt>Turbo::Broadcastable</tt>.
# A subscription to this channel is made for each individual stream that one wishes to listen for updates to.
# The subscription relies on being passed a <tt>signed_stream_name</tt> parameter generated by turning a set of streamables
# into signed stream name using <tt>Turbo::Streams::StreamName#signed_stream_name</tt>. This is automatically done
# using the view helper <tt>Turbo::StreamsHelper#turbo_stream_from(*streamables)</tt>.
# If the signed stream name cannot be verified, the subscription is rejected.
#
# In case if custom behavior is desired, one can create their own channel and re-use some of the primitives from
# helper modules like <tt>Turbo::Streams::StreamName</tt>:
#
#   class CustomChannel < ActionCable::Channel::Base
#     extend Turbo::Streams::Broadcasts, Turbo::Streams::StreamName
#     include Turbo::Streams::StreamName::ClassMethods
#
#     def subscribed
#       if (stream_name = verified_stream_name_from_params).present? &&
#           subscription_allowed?
#         stream_from stream_name
#       else
#         reject
#       end
#     end
#
#     def subscription_allowed?
#       # ...
#     end
#   end
#
# This channel can be connected to a web page using <tt>:channel</tt> option in
# <tt>turbo_stream_from</tt> helper:
#
#   <%= turbo_stream_from 'room', channel: CustomChannel %>
#
class Turbo::StreamsChannel < ActionCable::Channel::Base
  extend Turbo::Streams::Broadcasts, Turbo::Streams::StreamName
  include Turbo::Streams::StreamName::ClassMethods

  def subscribed
    if stream_name = verified_stream_name_from_params
      stream_from stream_name
    else
      reject
    end
  end
end
=== stream_name.rb ===
# Stream names are how we identify which updates should go to which users. All streams run over the same
# <tt>Turbo::StreamsChannel</tt>, but each with their own subscription. Since stream names are exposed directly to the user
# via the HTML stream subscription tags, we need to ensure that the name isn't tampered with, so the names are signed
# upon generation and verified upon receipt. All verification happens through the <tt>Turbo.signed_stream_verifier</tt>.
module Turbo::Streams::StreamName
  # Used by <tt>Turbo::StreamsChannel</tt> to verify a signed stream name.
  def verified_stream_name(signed_stream_name)
    Turbo.signed_stream_verifier.verified signed_stream_name
  end

  # Used by <tt>Turbo::StreamsHelper#turbo_stream_from(*streamables)</tt> to generate a signed stream name.
  def signed_stream_name(streamables)
    Turbo.signed_stream_verifier.generate stream_name_from(streamables)
  end

  module ClassMethods
    # Can be used by custom turbo stream channels to obtain signed stream name from <tt>params</tt>
    def verified_stream_name_from_params
      self.class.verified_stream_name(params[:signed_stream_name])
    end
  end

  private
    def stream_name_from(streamables)
      if streamables.is_a?(Array)
        streamables.map  { |streamable| stream_name_from(streamable) }.join(":")
      else
        streamables.then { |streamable| streamable.try(:to_gid_param) || streamable.to_param }
      end
    end
end

# Provides the broadcast actions in synchronous and asynchronous form for the <tt>Turbo::StreamsChannel</tt>.
# See <tt>Turbo::Broadcastable</tt> for the user-facing API that invokes these methods with most of the paperwork filled out already.
#
# Can be used directly using something like <tt>Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_remove_to :entries, target: 1</tt>.
module Turbo::Streams::Broadcasts
  include Turbo::Streams::ActionHelper

  def broadcast_remove_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_to(*streamables, action: :remove, render: false, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_replace_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_to(*streamables, action: :replace, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_update_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_to(*streamables, action: :update, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_before_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_to(*streamables, action: :before, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_after_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_to(*streamables, action: :after, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_append_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_to(*streamables, action: :append, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_prepend_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_to(*streamables, action: :prepend, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_refresh_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_stream_to(*streamables, content: turbo_stream_refresh_tag)
  end

  def broadcast_action_to(*streamables, action:, target: nil, targets: nil, attributes: {}, **rendering)
    broadcast_stream_to(*streamables, content: turbo_stream_action_tag(
      action, target: target, targets: targets, template: render_broadcast_action(rendering), **attributes)
    )
  end

  def broadcast_replace_later_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_later_to(*streamables, action: :replace, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_update_later_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_later_to(*streamables, action: :update, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_before_later_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_later_to(*streamables, action: :before, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_after_later_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_later_to(*streamables, action: :after, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_append_later_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_later_to(*streamables, action: :append, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_prepend_later_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_later_to(*streamables, action: :prepend, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_refresh_later_to(*streamables, request_id: Turbo.current_request_id, **opts)
    refresh_debouncer_for(*streamables, request_id: request_id).debounce do
      Turbo::Streams::BroadcastStreamJob.perform_later stream_name_from(streamables), content: turbo_stream_refresh_tag(request_id: request_id, **opts).to_str # Sidekiq requires job arguments to be valid JSON types, such as String
    end
  end

  def broadcast_action_later_to(*streamables, action:, target: nil, targets: nil, attributes: {}, **rendering)
    streamables.flatten!
    streamables.compact_blank!

    if streamables.present?
      target = convert_to_turbo_stream_dom_id(target)
      targets = convert_to_turbo_stream_dom_id(targets, include_selector: true)
      Turbo::Streams::ActionBroadcastJob.perform_later \
        stream_name_from(streamables), action: action, target: target, targets: targets, attributes: attributes, **rendering
    end
  end

  def broadcast_render_to(*streamables, **rendering)
    broadcast_stream_to(*streamables, content: render_format(:turbo_stream, **rendering))
  end

  def broadcast_render_later_to(*streamables, **rendering)
    Turbo::Streams::BroadcastJob.perform_later stream_name_from(streamables), **rendering
  end

  def broadcast_stream_to(*streamables, content:)
    streamables.flatten!
    streamables.compact_blank!

    if streamables.present?
      ActionCable.server.broadcast stream_name_from(streamables), content
    end
  end

  def refresh_debouncer_for(*streamables, request_id: nil) # :nodoc:
    Turbo::ThreadDebouncer.for("turbo-refresh-debouncer-#{stream_name_from(streamables.including(request_id))}")
  end

  private
    def render_format(format, **rendering)
      ApplicationController.render(formats: [ format ], **rendering)
    end

    def render_broadcast_action(rendering)
      content = rendering.delete(:content)
      html    = rendering.delete(:html)
      render  = rendering.delete(:render)

      if render == false
        nil
      else
        content || html || (render_format(:html, **rendering) if rendering.present?)
      end
    end
end

module Turbo::Streams::Broadcasts
  include Turbo::Streams::ActionHelper

  def broadcast_remove_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_to(*streamables, action: :remove, render: false, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_replace_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_to(*streamables, action: :replace, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_update_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_to(*streamables, action: :update, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_before_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_to(*streamables, action: :before, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_after_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_to(*streamables, action: :after, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_append_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_to(*streamables, action: :append, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_prepend_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_to(*streamables, action: :prepend, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_refresh_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_stream_to(*streamables, content: turbo_stream_refresh_tag)
  end

  def broadcast_action_to(*streamables, action:, target: nil, targets: nil, attributes: {}, **rendering)
    broadcast_stream_to(*streamables, content: turbo_stream_action_tag(
      action, target: target, targets: targets, template: render_broadcast_action(rendering), **attributes)
    )
  end

  def broadcast_replace_later_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_later_to(*streamables, action: :replace, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_update_later_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_later_to(*streamables, action: :update, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_before_later_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_later_to(*streamables, action: :before, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_after_later_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_later_to(*streamables, action: :after, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_append_later_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_later_to(*streamables, action: :append, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_prepend_later_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_later_to(*streamables, action: :prepend, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_refresh_later_to(*streamables, request_id: Turbo.current_request_id, **opts)
    refresh_debouncer_for(*streamables, request_id: request_id).debounce do
      Turbo::Streams::BroadcastStreamJob.perform_later stream_name_from(streamables), content: turbo_stream_refresh_tag(request_id: request_id, **opts).to_str # Sidekiq requires job arguments to be valid JSON types, such as String
    end
  end

  def broadcast_action_later_to(*streamables, action:, target: nil, targets: nil, attributes: {}, **rendering)
    streamables.flatten!
    streamables.compact_blank!

    if streamables.present?
      target = convert_to_turbo_stream_dom_id(target)
      targets = convert_to_turbo_stream_dom_id(targets, include_selector: true)
      Turbo::Streams::ActionBroadcastJob.perform_later \
        stream_name_from(streamables), action: action, target: target, targets: targets, attributes: attributes, **rendering
    end
  end

  def broadcast_render_to(*streamables, **rendering)
    broadcast_stream_to(*streamables, content: render_format(:turbo_stream, **rendering))
  end

  def broadcast_render_later_to(*streamables, **rendering)
    Turbo::Streams::BroadcastJob.perform_later stream_name_from(streamables), **rendering
  end

  def broadcast_stream_to(*streamables, content:)
    streamables.flatten!
    streamables.compact_blank!

    if streamables.present?
      ActionCable.server.broadcast stream_name_from(streamables), content
    end
  end

  def refresh_debouncer_for(*streamables, request_id: nil) # :nodoc:
    Turbo::ThreadDebouncer.for("turbo-refresh-debouncer-#{stream_name_from(streamables.including(request_id))}")
  end

  private
    def render_format(format, **rendering)
      ApplicationController.render(formats: [ format ], **rendering)
    end

    def render_broadcast_action(rendering)
      content = rendering.delete(:content)
      html    = rendering.delete(:html)
      render  = rendering.delete(:render)

      if render == false
        nil
      else
        content || html || (render_format(:html, **rendering) if rendering.present?)
      end
    end
end

**Analyzing the "Being Edited" Indicator Issue**

Okay, deep breath. This is a critical problem. We need to dissect this carefully, word by word. The core issue is that a collaborator removed from a book continues to receive "being edited" presence payloads, even after their access is revoked, because their WebSocket connection remains open. The goal: Fix this without disrupting the real-time indicator.

First, let's establish the current setup. The "being edited" indicator uses Turbo Streams via ActionCable.  A `turbo_stream_from` subscribes to a channel, and `broadcast_render_later_to` pushes updates. The current implementation uses a shared stream name (`[leaf, :being_edited]`) for all editors. A key observation: `Turbo::StreamsChannel#subscribed` only validates the signed stream name, *not* whether the user has edit access.

Here's the problem in a nutshell:

1.  User A (editor) and User B (collaborator) open the editor.
2.  User B's browser subscribes to the shared `Turbo::StreamsChannel`.
3.  User A removes User B's access.
4.  User A edits and saves, triggering a broadcast to the shared channel.
5.  User B's *open* WebSocket connection *still* receives the "being edited" payload because it's still subscribed to the shared channel and ActionCable broadcasts directly to active subscriptions.

The real kicker: "The payload must not go out on a channel a removed collaborator can still be listening on."  This means we need to prevent the payload from reaching disconnected users.

The core question is this: Why can a removed collaborator still listen on a channel?

There are two main areas to consider:

*   **Shared Stream:**  The current shared stream approach (`[leaf, :being_edited]`) inherently allows this to happen. Even if we disconnect/unsubscribe users when access is revoked, ActionCable clients *automatically reconnect*, especially if they have the signed stream name cached, *unless* channel subscription also checks access. ActionCable's `remote_connections` may not be robust enough to handle the disconnect, or could be asynchronous. This solution, even with disconnects, isn't foolproof.

*   **Per-User or Per-Access Streams:** The more promising avenue involves scoped streams.  Imagine if each editor subscribed to a *unique* stream, like `[leaf, :being_edited, Current.user]` or even `[leaf, :being_edited, access_id]`.  When broadcasting, the server would only send updates to those *currently* authorized.  When User B is removed, the server no longer broadcasts to `[leaf, :being_edited, bob]`. Even if Bob's browser is still open, it won't receive payloads because it's no longer receiving broadcasts, because it can't subscribe!

    *   When User A edits, the server *only* broadcasts to the streams of users who *currently* have editor access. This would solve the problem because if Bob is removed, his stream will not receive the payload!
    *   This approach seamlessly handles scenarios where someone is removed and re-added. The new subscription on re-addition would only be triggered if `Current.user` has access!
    *   This will handle admins:
        *   An administrator might NOT have an `Access` record for the book.
        *   Administrators who don't have an access for a book will have `access_for(user: admin)` be `nil`.
        *   We need to verify if these will still allow the correct behavior!

Let's test all these options in the codebase! This demands a deep dive into the code: searching for terms like `editable?`, `access_for`, `administrator`, `update_access`, `accesses`, `ActionCable`, `remote_connections`, and any related background jobs to understand the current implementation and how to adapt it to the per-user stream approach.

module Leaf::Editable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS = 10.minutes

  included do
    has_many :edits, dependent: :delete_all

    after_update :record_moved_to_trash, if: :was_trashed?
  end

  def edit(leafable_params: {}, leaf_params: {})
    if record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      update_and_record_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    else
      update_without_recording_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    end
  end

  private
    def record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      will_change_leafable?(leafable_params) && last_edit_old?
    end

    def last_edit_old?
      edits.empty? || edits.last.created_at.before?(MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS.ago)
    end

    def will_change_leafable?(leafable_params)
      leafable_params.select do |key, value|
        leafable.attributes[key.to_s] != value
      end.present?
    end

    def update_without_recording_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.last&.touch
        update! leaf_params
      end
    end

    def update_and_record_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        new_leafable = dup_leafable_with_attachments leafable
        new_leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.revision.create!(leafable: leafable)
        update! leaf_params.merge(leafable: new_leafable)
      end
    end

    def dup_leafable_with_attachments(leafable)
      leafable.dup.tap do |new|
        leafable.attachment_reflections.each do |name, _|
          new.send(name).attach(leafable.send(name).blob)
        end
      end
    end

    def record_moved_to_trash
      edits.trash.create!(leafable: leafable)
    end

    def was_trashed?
      trashed? && previous_changes.include?(:status)
    end
end

messages.thinking:
**Analyzing the "Being Edited" Indicator for Writebook**

Alright, let's break this down systematically. The core issue is that a collaborator removed from a book continues to receive "being edited" presence payloads, which leaks information and presents a security vulnerability.  The goal is to fix this without breaking the existing indicator.

First, let's dissect the current implementation.  The indicator is triggered when a user opens a page editor, rendering `being_edited_indicator`, which establishes a Turbo Streams connection. Currently, all editors share the same `Turbo::StreamsChannel` stream, identified by the leaf ID. There's no authorization within the channel's `subscribed` method, only cryptographic signature verification. When a user saves, `broadcast_being_edited_indicator` broadcasts to this shared channel, and every connected client receives the update.  The problem arises when a collaborator is removed – their open editor tab continues to listen on this shared channel.

Now, let's consider the key requirement: prevent payloads from going out on a channel a removed collaborator could be listening on.  This rules out solutions that only address the subscription phase (e.g., trying to reject the subscription in the `subscribed` method), because the problem is the existing, open subscription.  Disconnecting connections directly in callbacks is fragile and incomplete.

So, let's examine the design considerations. We need a robust architecture to solve this.

The cleanest approach, and probably the best design, seems to be to implement per-user streams.  Instead of a shared stream, each subscriber would subscribe to a stream specific to their user ID (e.g., `[leaf, :being_edited, Current.user]`).  At broadcast time, the server would identify the set of users who currently have edit access to the book.  When Alice saves, it broadcasts only to the streams associated with the current editors.  If Bob is removed, his open stream would receive *nothing*. 

We need to consider these scenarios:

*   **Per-user Stream**: The simplest solution that prevents broadcast to the removed editor.
*   **Authorization**: The crucial aspect is how we determine who should receive the broadcast. The code must determine active users with edit access at the broadcast time.
*   **Administrator**: The code must handle the case of administrators, who might not have an explicit access record for a book but still have editing privileges. The "per-user stream" option with a check of editable state is best because it includes the administrators without relying on explicit access.
*   **Custom ActionCable Channel**: We could use a custom channel, but that's likely unnecessary, though it adds a layer of authorization.

In summary, the most robust solution is to use per-user streams, such as `[leaf, :being_edited, Current.user]`, and ensure that broadcasts are only sent to those streams corresponding to users who currently have edit access. Using the per-user stream approach addresses the issue in a more secure and efficient way. We need to be careful, however, to check for both the user's role and book access when sending messages to avoid leaking information.

messages.content: Let's check ActiveJob's queue adapter in test and development, and check how `broadcast_render_later_to` behaves in tests.
messages.thinking:
**Deep Dive into Real-Time Collaboration Logic**

Okay, so I've been really digging into how we're handling real-time editing presence indicators, specifically to address that tricky scenario where someone gets removed from a book while their editor is still open. My goal? Ensuring those presence updates *only* go to users who are currently *supposed* to be seeing them.

First, I've got to revisit the core elements, `cable_stream_source_element.js` and `Turbo::StreamsChannel`. The documentation in `Turbo::StreamsChannel` is a great starting point, showing us how we can customize channel behavior, particularly using helpers like `Turbo::Streams::StreamName`. That example of `CustomChannel` looks promising, especially how it leverages `turbo_stream_from` to connect the frontend. And `TurboCableStreamSourceElement`? It's all about that `<turbo-cable-stream-source>` tag, which is setting the stage for how streams are established. That `signed-stream-name` attribute is crucial and worth understanding better in relation to authorization.

Now, let's nail down these key areas to trace: (1) per-user streams (or per-user-and-leaf streams), (2) custom channel authorization, (3) active subscription versus collaborator removal, and (4) the broadcast mechanism itself.

Scenario 1: Two editors, Alice and Bob, both open the page. Okay, so when Alice opens `/books/1/pages/1/edit`, we call `turbo_stream_from` to set up her stream (e.g., `[leaf, :being_edited, alice]`). Bob does the same, getting his stream, `[leaf, :being_edited, bob]`. When Alice saves, we need to broadcast a being-edited update. The code is already set up to include `hide_from_user_id: user.id`, which means she's not receiving her own presence information anyway.

Now, Scenario 2: What if Bob gets removed while he has the editor open? That’s the crux. If Alice removes Bob, the key is what happens when Alice saves. It’s all about the server determining *who* is currently allowed to edit, excluding (or, preferably, *including*?) the current user (Alice). Look at `Book#editable?` – the code already checks the access and administrator roles. The critical point is: Is Bob on that list *at the time* of the broadcast? If Bob's access is gone, NO broadcast will be sent to his stream, `[leaf, :being_edited, bob]`. Simple. Alice and the other active collaborators will still see active editors in their views.

Scenario 3: Bob tries to reconnect or forge a subscription? This is where the custom channel is important. Using `Turbo::StreamsChannel` alone might accept any valid `signed_stream_name`, BUT, a custom channel gives us more control. In our custom channel, when a subscription is requested, we can and *should* verify: 1) the current user is active, 2) that signed stream name is valid, 3) the stream name matches the current user, 4) the leaf and its book are both active, and 5) that the current user has editor access. If Bob is removed, his subscription will be REJECTED upon reconnect. Even if Bob somehow obtained a valid signed name, authorization should verify access and reject an unauthorized subscription. This is key to preventing those stale presence updates.

Scenario 4: Now, the race condition. What happens if Alice saves, the broadcast job is enqueued, and *then* Bob is removed before the job executes? This is where a dedicated job that runs at a later time (with `broadcast_render_later_to`) is super important. We should be using a dedicated `BeingEditedBroadcastJob` (or similar) that verifies the editors *again* at the time it runs. This way, if Bob is gone *when the job executes*, no message will go out to his stream. `broadcast_render_later_to` would not be sufficient.

The key to preventing those stale updates is the per-user stream approach: `[leaf, :being_edited, user]`. This allows a quick and easy way for each user to subscribe. When a user can no longer edit, no broadcast goes out to that specific user's stream. That's the solution.

One final note: In addition to a proper job, we should verify the user's eligibility *each* time a broadcast happens.

messages.thinking:
**Deep Dive: Building a Secure and Robust Being Edited Channel with Turbo Streams**

Okay, let's break this down meticulously. The goal is to create a channel, likely named `Leaves::BeingEditedChannel`, `Leaf::BeingEditedChannel`, or simply `BeingEditedChannel`, to manage real-time updates for leaf editing. The `Leaves::BeingEditedBroadcastJob` (or similar) will be a clean, elegant piece of the puzzle. We need to think about the custom channel, the appropriate stream name (and streamables), and how to handle scenarios like Action Cable disconnects, rejections, and remote connections.

First, the channel itself. We can start by examining the mechanics of `Turbo::StreamsChannel`. It leverages `turbo-rails` and the excellent `turbo_stream_from` helper, something like:

We should check how similar controllers, models, and channels in our codebase are named: this will help us be consistent and readable. In `turbo-rails/app/channels/turbo/streams_channel.rb`, we see that `Turbo::StreamsChannel` extends `ActionCable::Channel::Base` directly, with modules for broadcast and stream names.

This is critical! Our channel can inherit from `ApplicationCable::Channel` (which, itself, inherits from `ActionCable::Channel::Base`) and then extend the necessary `Turbo::Streams` modules. Inheriting from `ApplicationCable::Channel` is important because that already delegates the `current_user` method from the connection. We want to avoid writing more code than we need to.

Now, let's explore security. We want to make sure only authorized users are listening to these streams. The main question here is: what gets passed to `turbo_stream_from`?

We need to make it secure, tamper-proof, and easy to test.

We can pass the `leaf`, a symbol `being_edited`, and the `current_user` to the `turbo_stream_from` helper. In `app/views/leaves/_being_edited_indicator.html.erb`:

Or, even simpler! It's important to understand the `stream_name`. With `turbo-rails`, the `stream_name` will be derived from the `leaf` and the `current_user` using `to_gid_param`.

The stream name will be in the form of `"<leaf_gid_param>:being_edited:<user_gid_param>"`. We need to verify that a malicious user cannot craft a subscription with a different `leaf` than what they have access to.

**Important!**

We can have our `Leaves::BeingEditedChannel#subscribed` check:

1.  Is the user active? `current_user&.active?`
2.  Does a valid leaf exist? `@leaf = Leaf.active.find_by(id: params[:leaf_id])`
3.  Does the current user have access to the leaf? `leaf.book.editable?(user: current_user)`
4.  Is the `stream_name` verified? `verified_stream_name_from_params`
5.  Is the verified stream name equal to what we expect it to be? `stream_name == self.class.stream_name_from([leaf, :being_edited, current_user])`

Now the channel, when the user subscribes will:

def subscribed
  if current_user&.active? &&
      (leaf = Leaf.active.find_by(id: params[:leaf_id])) &&
      leaf.book.editable?(user: current_user) &&
      (stream_name = verified_stream_name_from_params).present? &&
      stream_name == self.class.stream_name_from([leaf, :being_edited, current_user])
    stream_from stream_name
  else
    reject
  end

We could even check whether we need to pass the `leaf_id` via `data-leaf-id`. Can we decode the `leaf` and `user` directly from the `signed_stream_name`? Splitting by ":" gives the GIDs. We can locate this with `GlobalID::Locator.locate(Base64.urlsafe_decode64(leaf_gid_param))`. However, why complicate things? The `data-leaf-id` is explicit and verifies the stream. It's safe!

Finally

messages.thinking:
**Security Analysis of Turbo Streams with Custom Channels**

Okay, so I'm looking at this implementation using `GlobalID.parse(param)` and thinking about streamlining it. The use of `turbo_stream_from` in `_being_edited_indicator.html.erb` seems interesting. It looks like it sets up a subscription with the `Leaves::BeingEditedChannel`. When `turbo_stream_from` renders, it generates a `signed-stream-name` encoded with the `leaf` and the `user`, signed by `Turbo.signed_stream_verifier`, and specifies `Leaves::BeingEditedChannel` as the channel.

Now, let's dive into `Leaves::BeingEditedChannel`. It's either an `ApplicationCable::Channel` or a `Turbo::StreamsChannel`. I'll compare them. I see `find_authorized_leaf` is crucial. The `verified_stream_name_from_params` parsing is key: it extracts the `leaf_gid_param` and `user_gid_param`.  `GlobalID::Locator.locate` finds the `Leaf`, and then some critical authorization checks are done.  Here's what I'm seeing:

1.  The `signed_stream_name` implicitly contains the `leaf` and `user` *without* needing a `data-leaf-id` attribute.
2.  `Turbo.signed_stream_verifier` is used for verification.
3.  The `Leaf` is located, and its active state is confirmed.
4.  It verifies the stream belongs to the correct user and the correct leaf.
5.  It verifies the user and leaf are active and the user has permission to edit the book.

This is good; It's enforcing robust security.

But here's a thought: let's brainstorm all edge cases!

**Case 1:**  What if something broadcasts to `Leaves::BeingEditedChannel`?  How does `Leaves::BeingEditedChannel.broadcast_render_later_to` (or `ActionCable.server.broadcast`) actually work?

Remember: `Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_render_later_to` calls `Turbo::Streams::BroadcastJob.perform_later`, which calls `Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_render_to`, which, finally, calls `ActionCable.server.broadcast`.  `ActionCable.server.broadcast` broadcasts to *any* channel that is listening to the specific `stream_name` string, not just the specified channel class. This is because ActionCable pubsub is keyed by the stream name string itself, not by channel class. So `Leaves::BeingEditedChannel.broadcast_render_later_to` and similar methods *only* send messages to those subscriptions that called `stream_from` with that particular stream name.

A major concern: could a removed collaborator take the `signed_stream_name` from the `Leaves::BeingEditedChannel` and manually connect to `Turbo::StreamsChannel`?  Well, even if they *did*, nothing would *ever* be broadcast to `[leaf, :being_edited, bob]` once they're removed! What if we also make the stream name inside `Leaves::BeingEditedChannel` different from `Turbo::StreamsChannel` (e.g., stream_from [ stream_name ] or stream_for [ leaf, current_user ] or Leaves::BeingEditedChannel.stream_name_for(leaf, user))?

**A Deep Dive into ActionCable Security and Broadcasts**

Okay, let's break this down methodically. First, I'm noting the tools at my disposal: `Turbo::Broadcastable::TestHelper` leverages `ActionCable::TestHelper`, which means I can leverage `broadcasts`, `broadcasted_to`, and the subscription's `streams` in tests. Excellent. I can verify that streams are *or aren't* being broadcasted as expected.

I'm keying in on `Turbo::SystemTestHelper` and the `turbo_cable_stream_source` selector. This selector, importantly, relies on the `SignedStreamNameConditions` to match the signed stream name. So, if I use `turbo_stream_from`, a `turbo-cable-stream-source` element is rendered with a signed stream name. I can now assert, using a selector, that these elements *are or are not* rendered as appropriate. The `TurboCableStreamSourceElement` then subscribes to the channel, giving me a point to check.

Now, let's get into the *really* interesting question. A user, who previously had access to a page (and therefore a subscription), is removed. What happens? My analysis:

1.  **Does the payload go out?** The broadcasting job (`Leaves::BeingEditedBroadcastJob`) *specifically* checks the editors on the book. If the collaborator is removed, they are no longer in `leaf.book.editors`. Therefore, no broadcast is sent to *their* stream. Precisely as it should be. The stream is user-specific, `leaves:being_edited:<leaf_gid>:<removed_user_gid>`.

2.  **What about disconnecting?** *This* is the tricky part. Disconnecting the whole ActionCable connection is a blunt instrument. It affects ALL open tabs for a user. If I disconnect a user, I might disconnect their connection to a different page. Better is to let a page stay open.

    *   **Without disconnection:** The old tab is still *listening* on a now-invalid stream. However, the broadcasting job won't send anything to that stream. If the user refreshes, or if ActionCable reconnects, `Leaves::BeingEditedChannel#subscribed` will reject the subscription due to access changes. Perfect. If the user is *re-added*, no problem, because on reconnect, the subscription is allowed.
    *   **Testing this:** Crucially, if I check for broadcasts with a per-user stream, there will be *zero* broadcasts to the removed user's stream. This is testable! I can assert *no* broadcast is sent to the removed user. At the same time, I can assert the *valid* collaborator receives the message.

3.  **The Subscription Rejection:** The `Leaves::BeingEditedChannel#subscribed` method checks: `leaf.active? && current_user&.active? && leaf.book.editable?(user: current_user)`. If these conditions aren't met, the subscription is rejected.

4.  **Security of the Stream:** Even if the old signed stream name is still around, it's useless for bypassing the channel's security.

    *   The `Leaves::BeingEditedChannel` checks the *current* user, not the old signed stream name. The broadcast job sends to a stream constructed from the `leaf` and the *current* recipient (not the removed user).
    *   Even if someone tries to directly subscribe to `Turbo::StreamsChannel` with the old stream name, the `broadcast_to` path for the `Leaves::BeingEditedChannel` is distinct. They will NEVER receive the payload.

    **This is airtight!**

    *   No subscription without edit access.
    *   No subscription with someone else's stream name.
    *   `Turbo::StreamsChannel` is completely isolated from the `Leaves::BeingEditedChannel`'s broadcasts.
    *   Removed users get *no* broadcasts.

    The remaining editors *do* see the broadcasts. All is working as intended.

**Additional Checks**

I'm now thinking about edge cases. Where is the `_being_edited_indicator.html.erb` partial used? What happens if `Current.user` is nil at render? I have to check the codebase to confirm.

**A Deep Dive into the "Being Edited" Indicator Logic**

Alright, let's break this down. First, good catch on that `GlobalID::Locator.locate(gid)` potentially raising `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`. That was a key point, and testing confirmed it! Using `Leaf.active.find_by(id: gid.model_id)` with a model check is indeed cleaner and avoids that exception while also filtering for active records. I like it.

Now, that logic to check `leaf.book.editable?(user: current_user)` is solid for authorization.

The real meat here is in handling collaborator removal. The old approach, broadcasting to a shared channel (`@leaf, :being_edited`), was problematic. A removed editor could still listen on the stream and receive those "being edited" indicators, even when they no longer have access. That's a no-go.

By moving to a per-user stream with `Leaves::BeingEditedChannel`, which streams for `[leaf, user]` the payload is only ever sent to current editors of the book. Disconnecting a single stream (the old channel) and unsubscribing a user from it will have no effect. A user's websocket connection across all other tabs/books needs to be preserved, not killed. We don't want to over engineer, and ActionCable does not offer a way to kill a single subscription only. That's a huge win! If a user is removed, they simply won't receive the updates because the payload is not sent on a channel/stream a removed collaborator is still listening to. This is the fix.

The fact that `PagesController`, `PicturesController`, and `SectionsController` inherit from `LeafablesController` and all use `broadcast_being_edited_indicator` means the solution works consistently across all leafable controllers. We need to be careful to make sure we do the same checks there as on the original code!

Next, if there's only one editor, that's fine. The new code efficiently checks for the existence of other editors before even rendering the partial or broadcasting. It avoids unnecessary work, and that's good. Using `.to_a` here isn't a problem; this is a small-team app, and even with more users, it's efficient. No need for `find_each` or `pluck(:id)`. Clean.

Testing the rendering of `ApplicationController.render` and the `dom_id` calls without `Current.user` confirms that our template is robust. No reliance on the current user context there.

We also need to consider what happens if a user is an administrator without access. This covers that. `leaf.book.editors` will still include admins, so they will be correctly subscribed. After they are demoted, they will no longer be listed as editors, and updates are not sent to them.

Finally, we covered the `ApplicationCable::Connection` and ensured that deactivating the user will properly disconnect their connection. Good. And we always ensure that we respect the project's established code style and security best practices with `rubocop` and `brakeman`.

1. `_being_edited_indicator.html.erb` uses `turbo_stream_from leaf, :being_edited` on the unauthenticated `Turbo::StreamsChannel`, which shares a single stream per leaf across all editors and never checks `editable?` on subscription.
2. `LeafablesController#broadcast_being_edited_indicator` broadcasts to that single shared stream `[ @leaf, :being_edited ]`, so any collaborator who opened the editor before being removed from the book continues receiving presence payloads (including editor names) on that open subscription.

Before making changes, let's run a quick script to reproduce the current buggy behavior in test mode.

class Leaves::BeingEditedChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  extend Turbo::Streams::StreamName
  include Turbo::Streams::StreamName::ClassMethods

  def subscribed
    if (leaf = find_authorized_leaf) && verified_user_stream?(leaf)
      stream_for [ leaf, current_user ]
    else
      reject
    end
  end

  private
    def find_authorized_leaf
      return unless current_user&.active?

      if stream_name = verified_stream_name_from_params
        leaf_gid = GlobalID.parse(stream_name.split(":").first)
        if leaf_gid&.model_name == "Leaf"
          leaf = Leaf.active.find_by(id: leaf_gid.model_id)
          leaf if leaf&.book&.editable?(user: current_user)
        end
      end
    end

    def verified_user_stream?(leaf)
      verified_stream_name_from_params == self.class.stream_name_from([ leaf, :being_edited, current_user ])
    end
end
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > app/jobs/leaves/being_edited_broadcast_job.rb
class Leaves::BeingEditedBroadcastJob < ApplicationJob
  discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError

  def perform(leaf, editor)
    return unless leaf.active? && editor.active? && leaf.book.editable?(user: editor)

    recipients = leaf.book.editors.where.not(id: editor.id).to_a
    return if recipients.empty?

    content = ApplicationController.render(
      formats: [ :turbo_stream ],
      partial: "leaves/being_edited_by",
      locals: { leaf: leaf, user: editor }
    )

    recipients.each do |recipient|
      Leaves::BeingEditedChannel.broadcast_to([ leaf, recipient ], content)
    end
  end
end
EOF

module Book::Accessable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_many :accesses, dependent: :destroy
    scope :with_everyone_access, -> { where(everyone_access: true) }
  end

  class_methods do
    def accessable_or_published(user: Current.user)
      if user.present?
        accessable_or_published_books
      else
        published
      end
    end

    def accessable_or_published_books(user: Current.user)
      user.books.or(published).distinct
    end
  end

  def accessable?(user: Current.user)
    accesses.exists?(user: user)
  end

  def editable?(user: Current.user)
    access_for(user: user)&.editor? || user&.administrator?
  end

  def editors
    User.active.where(role: :administrator)
      .or(User.active.where(id: accesses.editor.select(:user_id)))
  end

  def access_for(user: Current.user)
    accesses.find_by(user: user)
  end

  def update_access(editors:, readers:)
    editors = Set.new(editors)
    readers = Set.new(everyone_access? ? User.active.ids : readers)

    all = editors + readers
    all_accesses = all.collect { |user_id|
      { user_id: user_id, level: editors.include?(user_id) ? :editor : :reader }
    }

    accesses.upsert_all(all_accesses, unique_by: [ :book_id, :user_id ])
    accesses.where.not(user_id: all).delete_all
  end
end
EOF

class Book::AccessableTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase

    book.update_access(editors: [], readers: [])

      assert_not book.editable?(user: user) unless user.administrator?
    end

    assert book.accessable?(user: users(:kevin))
    assert_not book.editable?(user: users(:kevin))
  end

class Leaves::BeingEditedChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  extend Turbo::Streams::StreamName
  include Turbo::Streams::StreamName
  include Turbo::Streams::StreamName::ClassMethods

  def subscribed
    if (leaf = find_authorized_leaf) && verified_user_stream?(leaf)
      stream_for [ leaf, current_user ]
    else
      reject
    end
  end

  private
    def find_authorized_leaf
      return unless current_user&.active?

      if stream_name = verified_stream_name_from_params
        leaf_gid = GlobalID.parse(stream_name.split(":").first)
        if leaf_gid&.model_name == "Leaf"
          leaf = Leaf.active.find_by(id: leaf_gid.model_id)
          leaf if leaf&.book&.editable?(user: current_user)
        end
      end
    end

    def verified_user_stream?(leaf)
      verified_stream_name_from_params == stream_name_from([ leaf, :being_edited, current_user ])
    end
end
EOF
